name: Dirt Bike
description: A two-wheeled motor vehicle with a seat or saddle, built only for off-road use and not meeting federal on-road safety or emissions standards, such as an off-road e-moto. It can't be registered for the road, and in Pennsylvania's cities police may impound and courts forfeit one ridden on public streets.

restrictions.rule: Two wheels and a seat or saddle, designed and manufactured exclusively for off-road use, and not compliant with Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards or EPA on-road emissions standards; no limit on motor power or speed
restrictions.citation: Pennsylvania Consolidated Statutes Title 75 §3722(g), added by Act 92 of 2022

restrictions.rule: Excludes a vehicle registered or required to be registered for the road, a titled dual sport motorcycle, and an electric pedalcycle: 100 pounds or less on two wheels over 11 inches, with operable pedals, a seat and a motor of no more than 750 watts that stops assisting at 28 mph
Not registered for the road, and a vehicle that isn't registered may not be driven on a highway

Within a city, though not a borough or township, barred from highways, including their berm and shoulder, sidewalks and bike lanes, except to cross a highway directly at a right angle after a full stop, and a divided highway only at an intersection
Riding one there is a summary offense, fined $50 to $200 for a first offense and $100 to $300 after that, plus costs
Police may impound one ridden there until the case is decided, and it's subject to forfeiture once the rider is convicted
Not an all-terrain vehicle, so the ATV registration and riding rules don't cover it
